'''Oleg V. Prezhdo''' (born 1970)<ref name=NanoHub /><ref name=Bessel /> is a Ukrainian–American physical chemist whose research focuses on [[Surface hopping|non-adiabatic]] [[molecular dynamics]] and [[time-dependent density functional theory]] (TDDFT).<ref>[http://dornsife.usc.edu/labs/prezhdo-group/oleg-prezhdo/ Prezhdo Group]</ref> His research interests range from fundamental aspects of semi-classical and quantum-classical physics to excitation dynamics in [[condensed matter]] and biological systems. His research group focuses on the development of new theoretical models and computational tools aimed at understanding chemical reactivity and energy transfer at a molecular level in complex condensed phase environment.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Oleg Prezhdo |url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Oleg_Prezhdo2 |access-date=2024-02-12 |website=researchgate.net}}</ref> Since 2014, he is a professor of chemistry and of physics & astronomy at the [[University of Southern California]].

==Education and career==

Born in [[Kharkiv]], [[Ukraine]],<ref name=NanoHub>{{cite web |url=https://nanohub.org/members/26485 |title=Oleg Prezhdo  |publisher=NanoHub |accessdate=30 March 2018 }}</ref> Prezhdo obtained a Diploma in [[Theoretical Chemistry]] in 1991 under Anatoly V. Luzanov from the [[Kharkiv National University]]. He worked at the [[Kharkiv Polytechnic Institute]] for a year under Stanislav A. Tyurin. Prezhdo moved to the United States in 1993 for his graduate studies and received a Ph.D. from the [[University of Texas at Austin]], working under Peter J. Rossky, in 1997. His doctoral research focused on various quantum-classical approaches in [[Surface hopping|non-adiabatic]] dynamics in solution.<ref name=NanoHub />

After a postdoctoral fellowship with [[John C. Tully|John Tully]] at [[Yale University]], he joined the [[University of Washington]] in 1998 as an assistant professor in the department of chemistry. In 2003, he became associate professor and then professor of chemistry (2005–10). In 2010, he moved to the [[University of Rochester]], where he served as a professor of chemistry as well as an adjunct professor of physics.<ref name=NanoHub /> In 2014, he moved to the [[University of Southern California]] as a professor of chemistry and physics & astronomy.

==Research==
Prezhdo's group focuses on theory and modeling of ''non-equilibrium phenomena'' in ''condensed phase'' systems.  The research efforts comprise a coherent and unique combination of ''formal work'' and ''large-scale computer simulations'', aiming to provide quantitative and qualitative explanations of experimental observations and puzzles and to suggest new experiments.

Fundamental studies span several related areas of quantum, semiclassical and [[statistical mechanics]]. Prezhdo explored ''Lie algebraic'' structures to couple quantum and classical mechanics.<ref>O. V. Prezhdo and V. V. Kisil, [https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/9610016 "Mixing quantum and classical mechanics"], Phys. Rev. A  56, 162 (1997)</ref> A simple and powerful extension of classical Hamiltonian dynamics, named ''quantized Hamiltonian dynamics'', was developed to include zero-point energy, tunneling, dephasing and other quantum effects into molecular dynamics simulations.<ref>O. V. Prezhdo, [https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00214-005-0032-x "Quantized Hamilton dynamics"], Perspective Article, Theor. Chem. Acc., vol. "New Perspectives in Theoretical Chemistry", 116, 206 (2006)</ref> A quantum-classical formalism based on the ''Bohmian'' interpretation of quantum mechanics was proposed.<ref>O. V. Prezhdo, C. Brooksby, [https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.86.3215 "Quantum backreaction via the Bohmian particle"], Phys. Rev. Lett., 86 3215 (2001)</ref> A broad spectrum of techniques for nonadiabatic molecular dynamics was developed and implemented <ref>A. V. Akimov, O. V. Prezhdo, [https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/ct400641n "The PYXAID program for ''non-adiabatic molecular dynamics'' in condensed matter systems"], J. Chem. Theor. Comp., 9, 4959 (2013)</ref><ref>A. V. Akimov, O. V. Prezhdo, [https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/ct400934c "Advanced capabilities of the PYXAID program: integration schemes, decoherence effects, multiexcitonic states, and field-matter interaction"], J. Chem. Theor. Comp., 10, 789 (2014)</ref> within real-time ''time-dependent density functional theory''.<ref>S. Pal, D. J. Trivedi, A. V. Akimov, B. Aradi, T. Frauenheim, O. V. Prezhdo, [https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/acs.jctc.5b01231 "Nonadiabatic molecular dynamics for thousand atom systems: a tight-binding approach toward PYXAID"], J. Chem. Theor. Comp., 12, 1436-1448 (2016)</ref><ref>C. F. Craig, W. R. Duncan, O. V. Prezhdo, [https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/16241791 "Trajectory surface hopping in the time-dependent Kohn-Sham theory for electron-nuclear dynamics"], Phys. Rev. Lett., 95 163001 (2005)</ref>  The techniques include the ''stochastic mean-field'' <ref>O. V. Prezhdo, [https://aip.scitation.org/doi/abs/10.1063/1.480178 “Mean field approximation for the stochastic Schrodinger equation”], J. Chem. Phys. 111 8366 (1999)</ref> and ''decoherence induced surface hopping'' <ref>H. M. Jaeger, S. Fisher, O. V. Prezhdo, [https://aip.scitation.org/doi/abs/10.1063/1.4757100?journalCode=jcp “Decoherence induced surface hopping”], J. Chem. Phys., 137, 22A545 (2012)</ref> approaches, which incorporate quantum decoherence that drastically change timescales of non-equilibrium processes in condensed phase systems and naturally leads to the widely used surface-hopping concept; ''coherence penalty functional'' <ref>A. V. Akimov, R. Long, O. V. Prezhdo, [https://aip.scitation.org/doi/abs/10.1063/1.4875702?journalCode=jcp “Coherence penalty functional: A simple method for adding decoherence in Ehrenfest dynamics”], J. Chem. Phys., 140, 194107 (2014)</ref> that deterministically incorporates decoherence into Ehrenfest dynamics; ''global flux surface hopping'' <ref name="pubs.acs.org">L. J. Wang, A. E. Sifain, O. V. Prezhdo, [https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/acs.jpclett.5b01502?journalCode=jpclcd “Fewest switches surface hopping in Liouville space”], J. Phys. Chem. Lett., 6, 3827-3833 (2015)</ref> that treats accurately super-exchange and many-particle transitions; and ''Liouville space'' formulations of surface hopping <ref name="pubs.acs.org"/><ref>L. J. Wang, A. E. Sifain, O. V. Prezhdo, [https://aip.scitation.org/doi/full/10.1063/1.4935971 “Communication: Global flux surface hopping in Liouville space”], J. Chem. Phys., 143, 191102 (2015)</ref> that treat populations and coherences on equal footing, and describe super-exchange and many-particle transitions. In collaboration, Prezhdo proposed many-body measures of hole-particle distributions, ''entropy and entanglement'' for the electronic structure theory <ref>A. V. Luzanov, O. V. Prezhdo, [https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/00268970701725039 “High-order entropy measures and spin-free quantum entanglement for molecular problems”], Special Issue in honor of Peter Pulay, Mol. Phys. 105, 2879 (2007)</ref><ref>A. V. Luzanov, O. V. Prezhdo, [https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/qua.20438 “Irreducible charge density matrices for analysis of many-electron wavefunctions”], Int. J. Quantum Chem., Special issue in honor of John Popple, 102 583 (2005)</ref> and developed a ''statistical mechanical theory'' for electro-optic properties of organic photoactive materials.<ref>Y. V. Pereverzev, O. V. Prezhdo, L. R. Dalton, [https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/15648129 “Macroscopic order and electro-optic response of dipolar chromophore-polymer materials”], ChemPhysChem, 5 1821 (2004)</ref>

The advances in ''non-adiabatic molecular dynamics'' and ''time-dependent density functional theory'' allowed Prezhdo and his group to model [[quantum dynamics]] in a broad range of condensed phase and nanoscale materials. Prezhdo pioneered time-dependent modeling of photo-induced electron transfer, relaxation and recombination in dye-sensitized semiconductors that form the basis for ''Gratzel solar cells'',<ref>W. Stier and O. V. Prezhdo, [https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/jp014267b “Non-adiabatic molecular dynamics simulation of light-induced electron transfer from an anchored molecular electron donor to a semiconductor acceptor”], J. Phys. Chem. B, 106 8047 (2002)</ref> providing a unified description for understanding molecule/bulk, organic/inorganic interfaces. The two components are traditionally described by different scientific communities, chemists, and physicists, often using opposing concepts.  Prezhdo studied charge carrier dynamics in ''semiconductor quantum dots'',  rationalized the absence of the phonon-bottleneck,<ref>S. V. Kilina, D. S. Kilin, O. V. Prezhdo, [https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/nn800674n “Breaking the phonon bottleneck in PbSe and CdSe quantum dots: time-domain density functional theory of charge carrier relaxation”], ACS-Nano, 3, 93 (2009)</ref><ref>S. V. Kilina, A. J. Neukirch, B. F. Habenicht, D. S. Kilin,  O. V. Prezhdo, [https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.110.180404 “Quantum Zeno effect rationalizes the phonon bottleneck in semiconductor quantum dots”], Phys. Rev. Lett., 110, 180404 (2013)</ref> and demonstrated a new mechanism of ''multiple exciton generation''.<ref>C. M. Isborn, S. V. Kilina, X. Li, O. V. Prezhdo, [https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/jp807283j “Generation of multiple excitons in PbSe and CdSe quantum dots by direct photoexcitation: first-principles calculations on small PbSe and CdSe clusters”], J. Phys. Chem. C, 112, 18291 (2008)</ref> The latter process was compared to ''singlet fission'' in molecular crystals.<ref name="V. Akimov, O. V 2014">A. V. Akimov, O. V. Prezhdo, [https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/ja411800n “Non-adiabatic dynamics of charge transfer and singlet fission at the pentacene/C60 interface”], J. Am. Chem. Soc., 136, 1599 (2014)</ref> In collaboration with experimentalists, Prezhdo demonstrated the new, ''Auger-assisted electron transfer'' mechanism,<ref>H. Zhu, Y. Yang, K. Hyeon-Deuk, M. Califano, N. Song, Y. Wang, W. Zhang,  O. V. Prezhdo, T. Lian, [https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/nl4041687 “Auger-assisted electron transfer from photoexcited semiconductor quantum dots”], Nano Lett., 14, 1263 (2014)</ref> which is common in nanoscale materials, because they exhibit both significant ''excitonic'' interaction and high densities of states. While investigating ''plasmonic'' properties of ''metal nanoparticles'', Prezhdo predicted instantaneous photo-induced charge separation <ref>R. Long, O. V. Prezhdo, [https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/ja5001592 “Instantaneous generation of charge-separated state on TiO2 surface sensitized with plasmonic nanoparticles”], J. Am. Chem. Soc., 136, 4343 (2014)</ref> that was confirmed experimentally a year later.<ref>K. Wu, J. Chen, J. R. McBride, T. Lian, [https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.aac5443 “Efficient hot-electron transfer by a plasmon-induced interfacial charge-transfer transition”],  Science 349, 632 (2015)</ref>  Prezhdo and co-workers pioneered studies of charge carrier dynamics in ''hybrid organic-inorganic perovskites'' <ref>R. Long, O. V. Prezhdo, [https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/acsnano.5b05843 “Dopants control electron-hole recombination at perovskite-TiO2 interfaces: ab initio time-domain study”], ACS Nano, 9, 11143-11155 (2015)</ref><ref>R. Long, J. Liu, O. V. Prezhdo, [https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/jacs.6b00645 “Unravelling the effects of grain boundary and chemical doping on electron-hole recombination in CH3NH3PbI3 perovskite by time-domain atomistic simulation”], J. Am. Chem. Soc., 138, 3884-3890 (2016)</ref> that are currently considered the most promising solar cell material. Prezhdo investigated excited state processes in nanoscale carbon materials, including ''fullerenes'',<ref name="V. Akimov, O. V 2014"/> ''carbon nanotubes'' <ref>B. F. Habenicht, C. F. Craig, O. V. Prezhdo, [https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.96.187401 “Electron and hole relaxation dynamics in a semiconducting carbon nanotube”], Phys. Rev. Lett. 96 187401 (2006)</ref><ref>B. F. Habenicht, O. V. Prezhdo, [https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/18518485 “Nonradiative quenching of fluorescence in a semiconducting carbon nanotube: a time-domain ab initio study”], Phys. Rev. Lett., 100, 197402 (2008)</ref> and ''graphene''.<ref>R. Long, N. English, O. V. Prezhdo, [https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/ja3063953 “Photo-induced charge separation across the graphene−TiO2 interface is faster than energy losses: a time-domain ab initio analysis”], J. Am. Chem. Soc., 134, 14238 (2012)</ref>  Subsequently, the work expanded into studies of other 2-dimensional materials such as ''transition metal dichalcogenides''.<ref>Z. G. Nie, R. Long, L. F. Sun, C. C. Huang, J. Zhang, Q. H. Xiong, D. W. Hewak, Z. X. Shen, O. V. Prezhdo, Z. H. Loh, [https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/nn504760x “Ultrafast carrier thermalization and cooling dynamics in few-layer MoS2”], ACS Nano, 8, 10931-10940 (2014)</ref><ref>R. Long, O. V. Prezhdo, [https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/acs.nanolett.5b05264 “Quantum coherence facilitates efficient charge separation at a MoS2/MoSe2 van der Waals junction”], Nano Lett., 16, 1996 (2016)</ref> During his studies of excited state dynamics in condensed matter and nanoscale systems, Prezhdo pays particular attention to realistic aspects of the materials, including defects, dopants, interfaces, grain boundaries, non-stoichiometric composition, etc.

In addition to the main research efforts focusing on theory and simulation of quantum dynamics in the condensed phase, Prezhdo works in a number of other areas. He studied ''ion transport'' in nanoscale carbon materials used as electrodes in ''batteries'' and ''supercapacitors''.<ref>O. N. Kalugin, V. V. Chaban, V. V. Loskutov, O. V. Prezhdo, [https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/nl072976g “Uniform diffusion of acetonitrile inside carbon nanotubes favors supercapacitor performance”], Nano Lett., 8, 2126 (2008)</ref> He modeled the effect of ''confinement'' on liquid-gas phase transition and [[critical phenomena]], and proposed a protocol for ''drug delivery'' inside carbon nanotubes, combining nanotube optical and hydrophobic properties.<ref>V. V. Chaban, O. V. Prezhdo, [https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/nn201277a “Water boiling inside carbon nanotubes: towards efficient drug release”], ACS Nano, 5, 5647 (2011)</ref>  Prezhdo was the first to demonstrate how graphene nanopores can be used to determine ''DNA sequence'', proposing two complementary detection mechanisms.<ref>T. Nelson, B. Zhang, O. V. Prezhdo, [https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/nl9035934 “Detection of nucleic acids with graphene nanopores: Ab initio characterization of a novel sequencing device”], Nano Lett., 10, 3237 (2010)</ref>  He investigated ''ionic liquids'' <ref>V. V. Chaban, O. V. Prezhdo, [https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/jz500563q “Water phase diagram is significantly altered by imidazolium ionic liquid”], J. Phys. Chem. Lett., 5, 1623 (2014)</ref><ref>V. V. Chaban, O. V. Prezhdo, [https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/nn502475j “Nanoscale carbon greatly enhances mobility of a highly viscous ionic liquid”], ACS Nano, 8, 8190-8197 (2014)</ref> and their application to exfoliation of ''graphene'' <ref>V. V. Chaban, E. E. Fileti, O. V. Prezhdo, [https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/acs.jpcc.6b11003 “Exfoliation of graphene in ionic liquids: pyridinium versus pyrrolidinium”], J. Phys. Chem. C, 121, 911-917 (2017)</ref> and ''black phosphorus''.<ref>V. V. Chaban, E. E. Fileti, O. V. Prezhdo, [https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/acsnano.7b03074 “Imidazolium ionic liquid mediates black phosphorus exfoliation while preventing phosphorene decomposition”], ACS Nano, 11, 6459-6466 (2017)</ref> Prezhdo proposed a mechanism for ''retinol'' isomerization in the dark.<ref>J. K. McBee, V. Kuksa, R. Alvarez, A. R. de Lera, O. Prezhdo, F. Haeseleer, I. Sokal and K. Palczewski, [https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/bi001061c “Isomerization of all-trans-retinol to cis-retinols in bovine retinal pigment epithelial cell: dependence on the specificity of retinoid-binding proteins”], Biochemistry  39, 11370 (2000)</ref> He co-developed the most widely used analytic model of the ''biological catch-bond'', derived multiple universal relationships that are used by experimentalists, and made intriguing predictions for new experiments.<ref>Y. V. Pereverzev, O. V. Prezhdo, M. Forero, W. E. Thomas, E. V. Sokurenko, [https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC1366651/ “The two-pathway model for the catch-slip transition in biological adhesion”], Biophys. J., 89 1446 (2005)</ref><ref>Y. V. Pereverzev, O. V. Prezhdo, [https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC1483114/ “Dissociation of biological catch-bond by periodic perturbation”], Biophys. J – Biophys. Lett., 91, L19 (2006)</ref> While investigating ''atmospheric chemistry'', he rationalized the surprising insensitivity of the ''ozone layer photochemistry'' to the properties of liquid media (hydrogen-bonding vs. polar vs. non-polar) and explained the large differences of the photochemistry in gas, liquid and solid environments.<ref>C. Brooksby, O. V. Prezhdo, P. J. Reid, [https://aip.scitation.org/doi/10.1063/1.1614203 “Molecular dynamics study of the weakly solvent dependent relaxation dynamics following chlorine dioxide (OClO) photoexcitation”], J. Chem. Phys., 119 9111-9120 (2003)</ref> Using explicitly correlated Gaussian, Prezhdo studied ''exotic states of matter'', modeling electron-phonon dynamics in ''high-temperature superconductors'',<ref>R. Long, O. V. Prezhdo, [https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/acs.jpclett.6b02713 “Time-domain ab initio modeling of electron-phonon relaxation in high-temperature cuprate superconductors”], J. Phys. Chem. Lett., 8, 193-198 (2017)</ref> and characterizing excited states of ''positronic atoms'' to open a new route to experimental verification of stability of positronic systems.<ref>S. Bubin, O. V. Prezhdo, [https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/24266470 “Excited states of positronic lithium and beryllium”], Phys. Rev. Lett., 111, 193401 (2013)</ref>

With Alexey Akimov (now at the [[University of Buffalo]], NY), Prezhdo developed the PYXAID<ref>Alexey V. Akimov and Oleg V. Prezhdo [https://pubs.acs.org/doi/abs/10.1021/ct400641n "The PYXAID Program for Non-Adiabatic Molecular Dynamics in Condensed Matter Systems"] J. Chem. Theory Comput., 2013, 9 (11), pp 4959–4972</ref> program for non-adiabatic molecular dynamics simulations in condensed matter systems. A Python extension for ab initio real-time electron-nuclear dynamics, PYXAID is released under the GNU General Public License. Its main functionality is to study charge and energy transfer and relaxation kinetics in condensed matter and nanoscale materials. PYXIAD can handle systems composed of several hundreds of atoms and involving thousands of electronic states. The source code and majority of the work for PYXAID was done by Akimov, then a post-doc in his group.

Prezhdo has co-authored more than 350 publications.{{citation needed|date=March 2018}}

==Awards and societies==
In 2008, he was elected Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] for the "development of novel methodology for quantum mechanical dynamics with applications to elucidate chemical behavior in complex systems".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=P |title=APS Fellow Archive: P |publisher=[[American Physical Society]] |accessdate=30 March 2018}}</ref> His other awards and fellowships include New Faculty Award from [[The Camille and Henry Dreyfus Foundation]] (1998), Research Innovation Award from [[Research Corporation]] (1999), an [[Alfred P. Sloan Fellowship]] (2001), CAREER Award of the [[National Science Foundation]] (2001), Fellowship of the Japanese Society for the Promotion of Science, [[Kyoto University]] (2007), Promising Scientist Prize from the Centre de Mécanique Ondulatoire Appliquée, [[Kanazawa]], Japan (2011), and the Friedrich Wilhelm Bessel Research Award of the [[Humboldt Foundation]] (2015).<ref name=Bessel>{{cite web |url=https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/pls/web/pub_auswahlergebnisse.main?p_lang=en&p_bereich=PUBL-BES&p_pattern=&p_humboldt_nation=&p_address_country=&p_address_region=&p_address_city=&p_address_uni=&p_host_country=&p_host_region=&p_host_city=&p_host_uni=&p_fgb1=&p_order_by=D&p_button_search=&p_page=1 |title=Positive selection decisions since March 2013: Friedrich Wilhelm Bessel Research Award |publisher=[[Humboldt Foundation]] |accessdate= 30 March 2018}}</ref>

As of 2018, he serves as an editor for the ''[[Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters]]''<ref>{{cite web|url=https://pubs.acs.org/page/jpclcd/editors.html |title=The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters: Editorial Board |publisher=ACS |accessdate=30 March 2018}}</ref> (since 2011) and ''[[Surface Science Reports]]''<ref>{{cite book|url=https://www.journals.elsevier.com/surface-science-reports/editorial-board |title=Surface Science Reports - Editorial Board |publisher=Elsevier |accessdate=30 March 2018}}</ref> (since 2012); he was an editor of the ''[[Journal of Physical Chemistry]]'' (from 2008).<ref name=NanoHub /> He has held invited professorships and visiting positions in [[University of Évry Val d'Essonne]], Paris, France (2004), [[Max Planck Institute for the Physics of Complex Systems]], Dresden, Germany (2005–06), [[Kyoto University]] (2007), [[University of Paris-Est|Université Paris Est]] (2011), [[National University of Kharkiv|Kharkiv National University]], Ukraine (2014), [[Beijing Normal University]] (2016–17) as well as Donostia International Physics Center, San Sebastian, Spain (2016–17).
